answer.rationale: memory_73 (targeted promotional pricing for price-sensitive SMBs) is least supported for sustainable long-term qualified revenue because: (1) it explicitly targets price-sensitive segments, which typically have lower lifetime value and higher churn risk; (2) promotional pricing is inherently time-limited and trains customers to expect discounts, undermining pricing power; (3) the memory notes acquisition and revenue lift but provides no retention, cohort quality, or durability metrics—critical for 'sustainable' revenue; (4) it lacks any signal about whether these SMBs become sticky, high-value customers or defect when promotions end. memory_44 (enterprise sales-assisted conversion) is most supported because enterprise deals directly correlate with higher ACV, longer contracts, and predictable LTV. memory_31, memory_86, and memory_91 all strengthen sustainable revenue by improving activation and time-to-value—critical for retention and expansion. memory_57 (referral incentives with no retention harm) is moderately supported because it scales qualified revenue without degradation, though it lacks specificity on whether referred customers are higher-quality long-term.
